title: DURATION-2: efficacy and safety of switching from maximum daily sitagliptin or pioglitazone to once-weekly exenatide

what_it_measured.text: This subsequent, 26-week, open-label, uncontrolled assessment period evaluated the safety and efficacy of (i) continued exenatide once-weekly treatment and (ii) switching from sitagliptin or pioglitazone to exenatide once-weekly.

dose.text: In the second, open-label phase of DURATION-2, randomised oral medications were discontinued and all patients received 2 mg exenatide onceweekly treatment; patients and investigators were not notified of original treatment.

Patients (n = 514) were originally randomised to one of three treatment groups by UBC Clinical Technologies (San Francisco, CA, USA) via an interactive voice response system: exenatide once-weekly (2 mg) subcutaneous injection

route.text: Methods Randomised oral medications were discontinued and all patients received exenatide once-weekly.

In the second, open-label phase of DURATION-2, randomised oral medications were discontinued and all patients received 2 mg exenatide onceweekly treatment; patients and investigators were not notified of original treatment.

Patients (n = 514) were originally randomised to one of three treatment groups by UBC Clinical Technologies (San Francisco, CA, USA) via an interactive voice response system: exenatide once-weekly (2 mg) subcutaneous injection

endpoint.text: This subsequent, 26-week, open-label, uncontrolled assessment period evaluated the safety and efficacy of (i) continued exenatide once-weekly treatment and (ii) switching from sitagliptin or pioglitazone to exenatide once-weekly.

Study endpoints included change from baseline to weeks 26 and 52, and change from week 26 to week 52, in HbA1c, patients achieving HbA1c targets of < 7.0% (< 53 mmol ⁄ mol) and £ 6.5% (£ 48 mmol ⁄ mol), change in fasting plasma glucose (target £ 7 mmol ⁄ l), body weight, fasting lipids, fasting insulin, systolic and diastolic blood pressure, cardiovascular risk markers (urinary albumin ⁄ creatinine ratio, B-type natriuretic peptide, high-sensitivity C-reactive protein and plasminogen activator inhibitor-1), safety and tolerability.
Mean change from baseline for efficacy endpoints was expressed as least square means.

reported_results.text: Patients who switched from pioglitazone to exenatide once-weekly maintained HbA1c and fasting plasma glucose improvements (week 52: −1.6 ± 0.1%, −1.7 ± 0.3 mmol ⁄ l), with significant weight reduction (−3.0 ± 0.3 kg).

Evaluable patients who switched from sitagliptin to exenatide once-weekly demonstrated significant incremental improvements in HbA1c (−0.3 ± 0.1%), fasting plasma glucose (−0.7 ± 0.2 mmol ⁄ l) and weight (−1.1 ± 0.3 kg).

Results Evaluable patients who received only exenatide once-weekly demonstrated significant 52-week improvements (least square mean ± se) in HbA1c (−1.6 ± 0.1%), fasting plasma glucose (−1.8 ± 0.3 mmol ⁄ l) and weight (−1.8 ± 0.5 kg).

Patients who received exenatide once-weekly throughout the trial on average had a + 0.7 kg (P = 0.0325) increase in weight from week 26 to week 52, resulting in a −1.8 ± 0.5 kg (P = 0.0002) reduction from original baseline.

Patients who switched from pioglitazone to exenatide onceweekly exhibited a significant weight reduction (−3.0 kg; P < 0.0001; Fig. 3), such that body weight was similar to original baseline weight by week 52.

Patients who received exenatide once-weekly for 52 weeks sustained the initial 26-week improvements in HbA1c [least square mean change from original baseline (95% CI)] at week 52: −1.6% (−1.9 to −1.3%); Fig. 3.
